sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Automatic checks on every change
sections.what: Each time code is pushed or a pull request is opened, GitHub starts an Ubuntu machine with Node 22, installs packages, and runs typecheck, lint, tests and the production build in order. If any step fails, the check is marked failed.
sections.why: Likely reason: catches broken code before it reaches the main branch.
sections.watch_out: Packages are installed with npm install rather than npm ci, so versions may drift between runs.

summary: Automatic checks that run on every push and pull request to validate the code.
purpose: Catches type errors, lint problems, failing tests and build errors before changes are merged.
why: Likely reason: keeps the main code healthy as changes come in.
how: First, GitHub starts a fresh Ubuntu machine. Then it sets up Node 22, installs packages, and runs typecheck, lint, test, and build in that order. Each step must pass before the next one runs.
inputs: The repository code and the project scripts named typecheck, lint, test and build.
outputs: A pass or fail status on each push and pull request.
risks: npm install can pick up different package versions over time. Actions are pinned only to major versions. No caching, so runs are slower.
debug: Open the failed run on GitHub and find the first red step. Reproduce it locally with the same npm script. If packages differ between runs, compare the lock file.
